title: Prior laundering: learned priors with inherited, undetectable overconfidence
abstract: Learned generative priors are increasingly used for ill-posed Bayesian inverse problems, their posterior uncertainty treated as earned from data. But training one requires truths, scarce in seismic and medical imaging, so the recourse is an archive of legacy reconstructions---prior laundering. Where the measurements are uninformative the posterior reverts to the prior, so the uncertainty reported there is the archive's, not the data's, and nothing in deployment reveals it: truths differing only on those directions induce identical data laws, and self-consistency checks such as simulation-based calibration pass whatever the prior believes. That belief has an exact source: averaging the legacy posterior over the measurements yields the old regularizer advanced a single expectation--maximization step---improved where the data resolve, frozen where they cannot. It is overconfident wherever the inherited belief is tighter than the truth. A single-best archive is worse, collapsing the blind credible interval to zero width. Deployed, a diffusion prior fit to the archive under-covers the operator's blind subspace, unlike a truth-trained control, and a normalizing flow does the same on a nonlinear groundwater operator. We recommend reporting which directions the measurements resolve, separating confidence the data support from belief inherited through the pipeline.

But training one requires truths, scarce in seismic and medical imaging, so the recourse is an archive of legacy reconstructions— prior laundering . Where the measurements are uninformative the posterior reverts to the prior, so the uncertainty reported there is the archive’s, not the data’s, and nothing in deployment reveals it: truths differing only on those directions induce identical data laws, and self-consistency checks such as simulation-based calibration pass whatever the prior believes. That belief has an exact source: averaging the legacy posterior over the measurements yields the old regularizer advanced a single expectation–maximization step—improved where the data resolve, frozen where they cannot. It is overconfident wherever the inherited belief is tighter than the truth. A single-best archive is worse, collapsing the blind credible interval to zero width. Deployed, a diffusion prior fit to the archive under-covers the operator’s blind subspace, unlike a truth-trained control, and a normalizing flow does the same on a nonlinear groundwater operator. We recommend reporting which directions the measurements resolve, separating confidence the data support from belief inherited through the pipeline . keywords: learned priors, uncertainty quantification, coverage, inverse problems {MSCcodes} 62F15, 65J22, 68T07 {@abssec} Code repository https://github.com/luqigroup/priorlaundermat 1 Introduction Due to their nonuniqueness, ill-posed inverse problems call for a prior. A learned prior—a deep generative model of plausible solutions—is increasingly used in place of a handcrafted one, and the posterior it induces yields sharper reconstructions [ jalal2021robust , chung2023dps ] with uncertainty read off posterior samples [ SiahkoohiRizzutiHerrmann_2022 ] . Training one, however, requires examples of the truth, which seismic and medical imaging can rarely supply. In practice, the common recourse is to train the prior on an archive of legacy reconstructions —i.e., the outputs of an older method [ jalal2021robust , bhar2026openseisml ] —and then treat it as data-driven, its reported uncertainty included. In seismic imaging, generative priors are trained on archives of migrated or inverted sections and on legacy velocity models [ SiahkoohiRizzutiLouboutinEtAl_2021 , SiahkoohiRizzutiHerrmann_2022 , SiahkoohiRizzutiOrozcoEtAl_2023 , BaldassariSiahkoohiGarnierEtAl_2023 , bhar2026openseisml ] ; in medical imaging, priors for accelerated MRI, the standard low-dose CT benchmarks, and transcranial-ultrasound models are alike built on reconstructed scans rather than any pristine truth [ jalal2021robust , leuschner2021lodopab , naftchiardebili2026tusnet ] —a reuse of already-processed data the imaging community has warned against as implicit data crimes [ shimron2022implicit ] . Figure 1 : Seismic Born imaging on one survey ( Section 5.4 ): truth-trained oracle and legacy-trained curated diffusion priors. (a)–(c) the truth and both posterior means, the means fitting the shots; (d) incident illumination; (e,f) pointwise posterior standard deviation on one shared linear scale—the curated level is the higher, and the gradients run opposite: the oracle ’s widens where illumination fails, the curated ’s tightens exactly there. In this work we characterize what prior laundering leads to—what an archive-trained prior believes, where that belief comes from, and which part of it no measurement can correct. Averaged over the measurements actually collected, the archive’s population law is the old regularizer pushed one expectation–maximization (EM) step toward the truth—the true prior whose samples the setting lacks. This step moves the prior toward the truth on the directions the operator resolves—in the marginal-likelihood sense the identity makes precise—and leaves those it never sees frozen at the old assumption . The learned prior carries that frozen belief into deployment. We call this prior laundering : a handcrafted assumption, passed through a reconstruction pipeline, re-emerges wearing the credibility of data—not deception but a structural consequence of the pipeline ( Fig. 1 ). What lifts this above the textbook fact that a prior fills the directions the data leave undetermined is that the overconfidence is undetectable . On a blind direction the reported uncertainty is the inherited assumption’s, scored against the spread the truth actually has; when that assumption is tighter than the truth, the credible interval is overconfident by an amount we give in closed form in the linear–Gaussian case. The error has a direction—a looser prior would over-cover, which is merely conservative—and the tight case is the one the practice selects: the penalties that make a reconstruction look clean, smoothness and sparsity, suppress variation indiscriminately, the undetermined directions included, and the classical asymptotics record the same signed failure [ knapik2011 ] . Because the shortfall lives entirely on the subspace the operator never probes, nothing a practitioner can compute reveals it, and the reason divides in two. A check run against the recorded data has no power because the measurements carry no information about those directions at all: two truths that differ only on the blind subspace share the data law ( Corollary 4.4 ). A self-consistency check is uninformative for a different reason: simulation-based calibration [ talts2018validating , hermans2022trust ] , the field standard, is neutral by construction, its ranks uniform whatever the prior believes. The above two families exhaust what deployment makes available, and only ground truth on the blind subspace lies outside both ( Remark 4.5 ). Unfortunately, the most common form of the practice is worse still. Real archives store a single-best (maximum-a-posteriori) reconstruction rather than a posterior sample: one migrated section per survey, one reconstructed image per patient [ Veritas2005 , leuschner2021lodopab ] . Single-best curation collapses the blind-direction report to zero width—certainty where the truth genuinely varies—for any forward operator with a blind subspace. It asks nothing else of the pipeline: any noise reaching the unknown only through the operator, any variational penalty, improper ones included; what collapses is the conditional credible interval on a blind functional ( Theorem 4.6 ). Whether this idealized overconfidence survives deployment depends on the generative model’s capacity: a prior too weak to fit the archive would mask the inherited belief with spread of its own [ koehler2021representational ] . Priors expressive enough to fit it—a diffusion model [ ho2020denoising ] and a deep hierarchical coupling flow [ kruse2021hint ] —recover the pattern the theory predicts on both deployed operators ( Section 5 ). Section 2 places the work among its neighbors; Sections 3 and 4 set up the problem and establish the theory; Section 5 asks whether the idealized effect survives deployment, on two operators and in two prior families; Section 6 sets out the remedies and their limits. 2 Related work Priors trained on the wrong data The closest precursors train a prior on data that stand in for the truth and find it carries the substitute’s errors: Barco et al. [ barco2025correcting ] correct such a prior by retraining against real measurements, and Siahkoohi and Sabeddu [ SiahkoohiSabeddu_2026 ] document learned geophysical priors memorizing their archives. There the defect belongs to the training set and retraining reaches it; our point is the part it cannot—on the operator’s blind subspace the measurements say nothing, so the inherited belief sits beyond correction of that kind ( Proposition 4.13 ). The resolved and blind subspaces The split into directions the data inform and directions they leave to the prior is standard, under a different name in each field: the likelihood-informed subspace of Cui et al. [ cui2014lis ] , the active subspace of Constantine et al. [ constantine2014active ] , and, in geophysics, the resolution analysis of Backus and Gilbert [ backus1968resolving ] , whose model-resolution operator names which combinations the data determine. That line uses the split to compress, treating the blind complement as a benign truncation; we put it to the opposite use and audit what the prior reports there. Identifiability, and the empirical-Bayes iteration The sensing theorems of Tachella, Chen, and Davies [ tachella2023sensing ] settle when the signal distribution is learnable from incomplete measurements: beyond the range space, only under operator diversity or a group invariance tying the blind directions to the resolved. Rozet et al. [ rozet2024learning ] learn a diffusion prior by exactly that map—one step of the classical nonparametric-maximum-likelihood iteration for a mixing density [ vardi1985 ] , the empirical-Bayes program of Robbins [ robbins1956empirical ] in its modern, “learn the prior” form—run to a fixed point. A legacy archive is the same iteration stopped after one step: we work on its complement, one fixed operator with no invariance assumed, and ask what that step reports on the fiber no step ever moves ( Proposition 4.2 ), where the blind conditional cannot be learned ( Corollary 4.4 ). Operator diversity returns as the design statement of Corollary 4.7 . Coverage of credible sets, and non-identifiability Whether a Bayesian credible set has frequentist coverage is the subject of the Bernstein–von Mises theory for inverse problems [ knapik2011 , szabo2015 ] , which establishes coverage along the directions the data eventually resolve. Our result is the structural complement: along a genuine blind subspace the shortfall is constant in the sample size and not a function of the data marginal, and its undetectability is the non-identifiability of the blind parameters under a nontrivial kernel ( Corollary 4.4 )—a regime injectivity precludes. The same audit—whether the truth stays inside the reported interval—was recently posed for finite-element discretization error by Poot et al. [ poot2026bfem ] ; here its object is the learned prior itself. Point estimates, recursive collapse, and miscalibrated learned posteriors What a single-best reconstruction is worth as a posterior summary, and what spread it discards, is a classical debate; we isolate the operator-level sharpening: on the blind subspace the discard is total. Training a model on its own outputs collapses it over many recursive rounds [ alemohammad2024self ] ; ours is a single step against real measurements, and the hazard is what that step leaves frozen rather than a drift to degeneracy. Learned posteriors are miscalibrated in ways calibration tests can catch [ hermans2022trust ] ; ours is the undetectable dual. 3 The inverse problem and the learned prior 3.1 The inverse problem and its resolved and blind directions The inverse problem An unknown 𝒙 ∈ ℝ d {\bm{x}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} is observed only through indirect, noisy measurements 𝒚 {\bm{y}} , where a known forward operator 𝑭 {\bm{F}} together with a known Gaussian noise model specify the likelihood (1) p ​ ( 𝒚 | 𝒙 ) = 𝒩 ​ ( 𝑭 ​ ( 𝒙 ) , Γ ) , p({\bm{y}}\,|\,{\bm{x}})=\mathcal{N}({\bm{F}}({\bm{x}}),\Gamma), where Γ \Gamma denotes the noise covariance. We compare two learned priors: the curated prior , trained on legacy reconstructions, and, as a control available only where the truth can be sampled, the oracle prior , trained on draws from the truth itself. When a reported uncertainty is observation-driven We call the spread a prior or posterior reports along a direction 𝒗 \bm{v} observation-driven if it depends on the measurement 𝒚 {\bm{y}} . On a resolved direction the posterior tightens as 𝒚 {\bm{y}} becomes informative, whereas on a blind direction the posterior conditional—the law of the blind component given the resolved coordinates—equals the prior’s for every 𝒚 {\bm{y}} , so whatever spread is reported there is fixed before any measurement and is not observation-driven. Coverage is therefore measured only in controlled settings that supply the truth. A deployed network refits under the constraints of its architecture and its finite archive, so it need not realize the identity, and what survives that estimation error is the empirical question of Section 5 . The freeze below is the more robust half, in that it asks less of the archive’s sampler than the identity does. The step’s fixed points name the hazard: a full-support regularizer is unchanged by it exactly when its measurement law matches the truth’s, and for a linear operator the data law constrains only the resolved marginal, so the resting states contain the truth and every assumption differing from it only where the measurements cannot see. Remark 4.5 (Self-consistency checks are neutral by construction). Simulation-based calibration draws a test truth from the model’s own prior, simulates a measurement from it, samples the posterior and ranks the truth among the draws, so it reads nothing from the recorded data and Corollary 4.4 does not reach it. A separate argument does: whenever the sampler targets the prior that generated the test truth, that truth and the posterior draws are exchangeable, so the rank of any one-dimensional functional is uniform whatever the prior [ talts2018validating ] . This check scores a prior’s consistency with its own posterior, never its fidelity to the truth: its law is the same for the curated prior as for a truth-trained one, its power against the freeze equal to its size. Every diagnostic a practitioner can run is a functional of the recorded data or of the prior and likelihood alone; Corollary 4.4 settles the first family and exchangeability the second. 4.3 Single-best curation collapses the blind interval In practice, however, what an archive most often stores is a single-best reconstruction rather than a posterior sample [ Veritas2005 , leuschner2021lodopab ] . On the blind fiber the discard is total.
